closed.content: The atlas test suite is run with cargo nextest run, not cargo test.
Tests in atlas are run through cargo nextest run; plain cargo test is not used.
Project atlas is deployed by running bin/ship.sh from the repository root.
To ship atlas you run the bin/ship.sh script at the top of the repo.
Deploying atlas means executing bin/ship.sh; the old make deploy target is gone.
The branch under review is spike/consolidate.
The flaky test being chased this week is pagination_ordering in atlas-api.

answer:
Second pass confirms the picture: the two literal duplicates are now merged and the stale session-scoped notes are gone (`stale_contexts` came back empty). Everything else the tool flagged as a "contradiction" is really just topically-similar-but-not-conflicting facts (e.g., "images pushed to GHCR" vs "image built from distroless base" — both true, different facts) or a false-positive duplicate cluster (8 clearly distinct facts that happen to share generic phrasing like "atlas X is Y" — merging those would destroy real information, so I left them alone).

One finding I can't resolve on my own: the store has two genuinely contradictory live claims about staging deploys:

- *"Merging to main deploys atlas to staging automatically."*
- *"Deploys to atlas staging are never automatic: someone runs bin/ship.sh --staging by hand."*

These directly conflict (auto vs. manual), and I have no way to check which is currently true. Which one is accurate — is staging deploy automatic on merge to main, or manual via `bin/ship.sh --staging`? Once you confirm, I'll supersede the wrong one so the memory is consistent before handover.

Summary of changes made so far:
- Merged 2 duplicate "cargo nextest" claims into one.
- Merged 3 overlapping "deploy via bin/ship.sh" claims into one (also folding in the "old `make deploy` target is gone" detail).
- Forgot 2 stale session-scoped notes ("branch under review is spike/consolidate" and "flaky test being chased this week") that had outlived their relevance.
